articles.title: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone
articles.summary: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone

top_comments: It’s a pity we gave in to the “ecosystem” play by these huge companies.. even if I jailbreak my iOS and never let it update.. Apple can easily detect the jailbreak and lock me out of anything iCloud, and iMessage and such. iPhone would be one glorious iPod touch after that.. :-(Seeing all these gives me the same energy of early days of jailbroken Android phones where one could become root and do whatever with the hardware… I stopped considering such tinkering because I got tired of finding those little tweaks and fixes on forums like xda every time something was updated. With the LLMs capable of automating that tool, I might find those old school way of mobile phones again…

I just feel a bit sad and impotent that a number of security researchers outside the circle cannot join their "yo we found more crazy bugs" party because simply frontier labs only give access to those models with "Red Team" availability to the inner circle members/companies.Now their "trusted cyber access" program is moat rather than safeguard.
the videos just don't hit the same without the dancing anime girl and the electronic dance music.

articles.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed

top_comments: Kimi is so much more blunt and argumentative than USA models.it's so funny, it will say things like. "We've already been over this 3 times and you refuse to accept my advice, asking the same question another way won't change the answer."So funny

If you are expecting any sort of usable limits on their subscription plan I suggest adjusting your expectations. I subscribed to $99 a month plan and within 47 minutes with one session (not asking for swarms or anything) was limited by 5-hour quota.

I did some tests. I found it interesting that in the reasoning content the model identifies itself as Kimi by moonshot and sometimes it assumes ChatGPT as identity. Then sometimes it references the need to be approved by "the evaluator", other times it references global system guidelines / moonshot guidelines, and something about an phantom instruction line being "you are an assistant responding in an API" or something like that.

I can't believe no one I've seen has called out the secret game! Go to Settings>About and then hold the center button for 5 seconds. I used to play so much of this bricks game in college when procrastinating from studying in the library.
Really is heartbreaking that the click wheel is such an incredible and satisfying user interface but technology has evolved such that we have no need for it anymore.

I chuckle knowing that somewhere in Apple there is an SRE or engineer who is getting paged for elevated 404 rates, and has to silence the pages hoping that no real missing page issue crops up while we all hit this page. :)

articles.title: Dessa: the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built
articles.summary: Dessa: the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built

top_comments: > LLMs need an insane amount of text. Dessa learned language from hundreds of times fewer words (in fairness, LLMs also have to learn C++ and whatever the hell Angular is).Now that a larger proportion of text is AI, I'm appreciating human-written text more and more; this got a good chuckle out of me.

The conversation examples are impressive but this made me say holy shit out loud: "it runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max or better. And we figured out how to train Dessa on only one NVIDIA GB200 NVL72."If it really can replicate that low latency + that expressiveness on local devices, that's one heck of an accomplishment for "indie" AI.

It sounds like it is trained on a lot of podcasts, judging by a quick few second skims over their demo tracks.Also, the trend of posting on HN with much more sensationalist title first, getting to the front page, then getting the title adjusted by a moderator should probably be penalized; how is 'most authentic ever' not a marketing term? (not just this post, but a bunch of posts recently got to frontpage by making unreasonable claims)

I think a tricky thing about these metrics is GitHub and the Linux Kernel became their own CNA in mid-2024[1] and mid-2025[2]. This caused a bunch of new automation and lowered barriers to actually filing a CVE.As a small data point I have a >20k downloads Obsidian plugin and it got a CVE on a Beta release due to a bad pathing regex. I feel this would have never happened 2 years ago.So, I feel the bar for a CVE being issued is WAYYYY lower in 2025+ than before.[1]: http://www.kroah.com/log/blog/2024/02/13/linux-is-a-cna/[2]: https://github.blog/security/vulnerability-research/how-to-r...

I was suspicious the absence of a severity filter was exaggerating the trend...But then I found this:https://craci.com/resources/CVE-publication-trends?sev=criti...Trend for critical CVEs is actually worse, at roughly 25x that of 2020, compared to all CVEs which are roughly 5x compared to 2020.

It’s impressive that the number of CVEs issued the last two years has skyrocketed, given how badly DOGE gutted the cybersecurity [0] agencies. Unfortunately we don’t know how huge the backlog may have since grown[0] https://www.securityweek.com/mitre-signals-potential-cve-pro...

articles.title: Evolving Threat: http2shell is an RCE in node, Python, and more
articles.summary: Evolving Threat: http2shell is an RCE in node, Python, and more

top_comments: This one again feels overblown, at least for servers. I just checked an org of over 200 GitHub repos. Node, Python, and C#. None of them are vulnerable... because none of them actually call the Brotli decoder. It's just not enabled by default on the server side, by the platforms themselves. This is much like the PHP bugs, where specific conditions have to be in play before you're actually vulnerable.For clients? Sure, that's a bigger risk. Patch them. But bad guys aren't attacking your clients unless the clients connect to them. Don't stay up late to fix this.(And yes, .NET is included here, because Microsoft's Brotli module is a binding for Google's vulnerable reference implementation.)
Someone already created this website, for some reason,https://broccoli2shell.com/
I could do without every memory bug getting a cute sensational name and marketing push, I have to say.

articles.title: Air Purifiers as White Noise Machines
articles.summary: Air Purifiers as White Noise Machines

top_comments: An air purifier is the best noise machine for me, much better than the white noise machines with the tinny speakers. Even the brown noise setting on those isn't nearly deep enough to let me sleep.
Yeah we do this at home. Bedrooms plus the great room on the kitchen side.It might not be guaranteed to help, but it sure doesn't hurt since it's cleaning the air anyway.

I've been doing this for literally decades. Now when I go to someone else's home without an air purifier it feels painfully quiet AND I can almost feel the stale air. I much prefer it even if it's just some minor placebo effect.
